Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with preserved contour, which is a classic radiographic sign of unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis (often due to phrenic nerve injury). While the left side appears somewhat irregular ("scalloping"), the dominant and most clinically significant finding explaining the asymmetry and elevation is right-sided paralysis, distinguishing it from effusion (which would show blunting/meniscus) or COPD (which causes bilateral flattening).
